newsitem.title: USA: POLL -- Cable seen trending down to Q4 and 1998.
newsitem.headline: POLL -- Cable seen trending down to Q4 and 1998.

text.p: Sterling strength against the U.S. dollar will have had its heyday by the end of this year as the United Kingdom's economic upturn comes to a top, some experts said.

Analysts in Reuters' quarterly economic survey forecast, on average, that the pound would slide to $1.6308 in the second quarter of 1998 from an average $1.6642 in the current quarter. Sterling strength may resume in the third quarter of 1998, although many pros surveyed said an extension of a negative trend was likely.

Growth in the U.K. and rising interest rates will inevitably come to a head, analysts said, and an economic turn would erode support for the cable trade. Sterling strength drawn from widespread forecasts for a weak single European currency will also begin to fade, they said.

"At some stage, probably next spring ahead of the final lock-in on the euro, the euro weakness story will get fully priced in," said Ron Leven, currency strategist at J.P. Morgan Securities. "Our forecast over the next 12 months is that the engine of growth is going to shift away from the Anglo block toward the core European block."
Because cable is ahead in the cycle -- U.K. rates began rising before U.S. rates -- it should conversely come off before the dollar, Leven said.

David Durrant, senior currency strategist at I.D.E.A., noted that strong cable will eventually hurt U.K. exports, prompting some degree of stall to the economy there. Further, an end to rising rates in the U.K. into 1998 will also tarnish the sterling, he said.
"We're getting the good strong data now, but as interest starts to tighten it up and they start to slow the economy you start to see softer data on the other side," Durrant said.

On a short-term basis, analysts called cable a "strong buy" even as it sits overvalued on a relative basis. But that overvaluation versus the dollar would become another drag on sterling as the economic cycle reverses, Leven said.

Victoria Marklew, international economist at Northern Trust Co, predicted there would be only a mild correction for the pound versus the dollar. That correction would also occur well into 1998, she said.

"(Sterling) is already overvalued, but I think the correction in 1998 is not likely to be that sharp given that you've got a lot of uncertainty over the European Union and interest rates are clearly going up in the U.K.," she said.
Marklew said she expects U.K. rates to rise at least through the middle of 1998. When the correction manifests itself, she said, the low point for sterling should not break below $1.60.

In the survey, cable forecasts for the third quarter of 1998 ranged from $1.55 to $1.72, with the mean at $1.6308. In the current quarter, experts marked a cable range between $1.62 and $1.6950, with the mean at $1.6642.
